comment: The filter is the same four-pole transistor ladder used in Retri, run at twice or four times the sample rate. The cutoff knob spans 40Hz to 4500Hz (Bass.cpp:43, :44) and the envelope's sweep is applied on top of it, with 31.37 per cent of the envelope below the resting frequency (Bass.cpp:39, :443); the result is clamped to 16Hz to 18000Hz (Bass.cpp:45, :46, :451). The ENVMOD menu item changes both the arithmetic and the parameter's own unit and multiplier at Bass.cpp:570 to :587, so the tooltip reads octaves or hertz to match; the setting is saved with the patch and an older patch loads with it off (Bass.cpp:286). Four more options are written and commented out of the menu: tuned resonance, first pole an octave up, passband compensation. The output is hard clipped at ±12V after a DC blocker that stands for the 303's output capacitor (Bass.cpp:461, :462). The accent is handled by extending the filter and amplitude envelopes rather than by a separate envelope; the maker's own comment at Bass.cpp:591 says the unused accent_env function was dropped for that reason.
